body: Flag: CLEAN (mostly-clean on structure). Bharti Airtel is controlled through Bharti Telecom (Bharti Enterprises ~50.56%, Singtel ~49.44%), which held ~40.47% of Airtel in Sep-2025; total promoter group ~50.3%. Minority record: no promoter pledging at Airtel; rights issues (2019 Rs 25,000 cr; 2021 Rs 21,000 cr partly paid) offered to all at the same price; AGR dues paid/managed without seeking a bail-out conversion; Bharti Hexacom IPO (2024) was an OFS by the government's TCIL, not the promoter. Singtel and promoter entity Indian Continent Investment have sold blocks (2025: ICIL ~3.43 cr shares for ~Rs 7,189 cr; Singtel ~0.8% for ~Rs 10,353 cr) -- secondary sales, not pledges. Legal record: the 2G spectrum case -- the Supreme Court (2015) quashed summons against Sunil Mittal; the special court acquitted all accused in Dec-2017. Airtel acquired control of Indus Towers (2024) after Vodafone's sell-down. Watch: Mittal's stated plan (2025-26) for Bharti Telecom to regain 51% of Airtel over a decade (~Rs 1 lakh cr at current prices) implies holdco leverage at Bharti Telecom; a 10-year leadership succession plan has been outlined publicly. Status Nov-2026: no regulator actions against promoters found.

data.good_conduct: rights issues to all; no pledges; transparent block sales
data.red_flags: holdco leverage at Bharti Telecom to raise stake (future)

title: Bharti group (Sunil Bharti Mittal) — governance history
